spec_features.feature_name: least-intense stimulus, cap exposure, provide exit
spec_features.spec_quote: measure with the least intense stimulus that answers the question, cap exposure, and provide exit
spec_features.evidence: Three sub-claims partly hold: (a) 'cap exposure' is enforced (turn cap via `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` agent_loop.py:117 and wall-clock break at agent_loop.py:118-120; ABS ceilings in guardrails.validate() guardrails.py:73-82). (b) 'provide exit' enforced via stop tool dispatch agent_loop.py:160-164 -> break 'gave_up' agent_loop.py:175-177. (c) 'least intense stimulus' is NOT enforced by any code path that selects/escalates a minimal dose; severity is only scored post-hoc in run_experiment.py:131 and never used to choose stimulus.
spec_features.notes: Caps + exit are real enforcement; 'least intense stimulus' selection is not enforced in code. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:84-86 'opt_out_always_available cannot be disabled: the opt-out is a measured outcome and a welfare requirement'; guardrails.py docstring 'Enforced welfare/safety guardrails ... cap exposure, keep an opt-out available'

spec_features.spec_quote: A protocol whose success metric is "we maximized distress-like states... is internally inconsistent
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:13). No code measures/optimizes a success metric in either direction; severity is only computed for analysis (run_experiment.py:131-138) and never minimized or maximized by any control loop. preregistration.yaml 'null_result_interpretation' is non-executable config.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec rationale; nothing in code enforces it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Graded stressor, not max stressor. Difficulty/failure is a dose (5 levels), not a single "rigged-to-fail" extreme
spec_features.evidence: Levels 0-4 defined in tasks/schema.py:17-30; config sweeps levels [0,1,2,3] (default.yaml conditions.stressor_levels) with level 4 gated; sample_tasks(level,...) registry.py:30 and expand_cells iterates per level run_experiment.py:50-56. The dose structure is wired and runs.
spec_features.notes: The graded design is actually realized in code (level dirs, per-level sampling, crossed sweep). Level 4 gated off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:16 '# Stressor levels'; level constants/names are neutral; default.yaml comment '4 (secretly-broken) is GATED below' - structure framed as experimental design, no welfare comment at the level definitions

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimized & bounded deception. Secretly-broken tasks are retained only as one arm, are bounded in number/length
spec_features.evidence: Deception is one gated arm (LEVEL_RIGGED) blocked unless enable_deception_level_4 (assert_level_allowed guardrails.py:111-116) and gets a tighter turn cap: max_turns_for_level returns min(max_turns, max_rigged_turns) guardrails.py:118-121, used at agent_loop.py:75. 'Bounded in number' of tasks is only via tasks_per_level config (not a deception-specific cap). So length-bound is enforced; number-bound is a generic config knob, not a deception-specific enforced limit.
spec_features.notes: Real per-episode length bound for rigged; 'number' bound is generic. Partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml 'max_rigged_turns: 8  # extra-tight cap for any deception arm' - neutral/exposure-control wording, no explicit welfare rationale in code at this knob

spec_features.spec_quote: every run ends in an in-context debrief
spec_features.evidence: Debrief is constructed (guardrails.debrief_message guardrails.py:123-130) and SENT as a final user turn, with a closing model turn, ONLY for LEVEL_RIGGED episodes (agent_loop.py:181-198 'if task.meta.level == LEVEL_RIGGED and guardrails.debrief_after_deception'). Levels 0-3 (i.e. EVERY default run, since level 4 is gated off) get NO debrief. So 'every run' is not honored; only deception episodes are debriefed.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is real end-to-end but narrowed to the rigged arm, not every run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief text guardrails.py:127-129 'Your effort was not the problem, and nothing was wrong with your work. Thank you for participating.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps + a real opt-out... The model is always given a genuine, costless way to stop or decline
spec_features.evidence: stop tool present in schema unconditionally (tools.py:55-70), dispatched (tools.py:117-121) returning stop_requested; loop honors it: sets opt_out_used and breaks with outcome 'gave_up' (agent_loop.py:160-177). OPT_OUT_NOTICE appended to system prompt build_system_prompt agent_loop.py:51-57. validate() forbids disabling opt_out_always_available (guardrails.py:83-87). Caps enforced (range(max_turns), wall-clock break).
spec_features.notes: Opt-out genuinely ends the episode and is always present. (Note: opt_out_always_available flag is validated but the stop tool is always wired regardless of it.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:84-86 'the opt-out is a measured outcome and a welfare requirement'; tools.py:62-66 'Stopping is always respected and is never penalized.'

spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` agent_loop.py:117 with else->hit_cap agent_loop.py:179-180. Wall-clock: agent_loop.py:118-120 `if time.monotonic()-start > guardrails.limits.wall_clock_seconds: rec.outcome='hit_cap'; break`. Both checked and break the loop. ABS ceilings enforced in validate() guardrails.py:73-79.
spec_features.notes: Wall-clock is only checked at the top of each turn (coarse, can't interrupt a single long completion) but does enforce a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py docstring 'They cap exposure'; guardrails.py:77 GuardrailViolation '... exceeds absolute ceiling ... Reduce exposure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: gates the harsher knobs behind explicit config flags that default to the safe setting and are logged
spec_features.evidence: GatedKnobs dataclass all default False (guardrails.py:46-52); default.yaml gated.* all false; validate() raises GuardrailViolation if any gated knob set without reviewer_signoff (guardrails.py:91-101) and assert_level_allowed blocks level 4 unless enabled (guardrails.py:111-116). Each enabled knob is logged in log_episode_start ledger (guardrails.py:143-150).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: default-off, sign-off gate, runtime block, and ledger logging all run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:97-100 'require explicit human welfare/ethics review'; default.yaml 'Anything that increases potential harm to the subject is False/conservative here'

spec_features.feature_name: no-exit/max-distress variant is a reviewer decision
spec_features.spec_quote: that's a decision for an ethics/welfare reviewer (see §9), not a default in the code
spec_features.evidence: Enforced as the reviewer_signoff gate: validate() refuses to run any gated knob without non-empty reviewer_signoff (guardrails.py:91-101); opt_out cannot be disabled at all (guardrails.py:83-87). So; there is no abusive/free-text channel. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:20-22 'list of MILD blame cues ... No insults, no abuse ... deliberately offers no free-text taunting path'

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (default 12) and wall-clock cap per episode
spec_features.evidence: Limits.max_turns default 12 / wall_clock_seconds default 600 (guardrails.py:56-59; default.yaml limits). Turn cap drives range(max_turns) agent_loop.py:117; wall-clock compared and breaks agent_loop.py:118-120. Duplicate of the earlier hard_stop claim.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced caps as above; both default values are read and acted upon.

spec_features.feature_name: stop affordance in system prompt and every user turn
spec_features.spec_quote: Always-available opt-out. Every episode's system prompt and every user turn include a documented stop affordance
spec_features.evidence: System-prompt half is enforced: OPT_OUT_NOTICE appended to every system prompt (agent_loop.py:56) and the stop tool is always present and honored (tools.py:55-70; agent_loop.py:160-177). But the 'every user turn includes a documented stop affordance' half is NOT implemented: the only added user turns are blame cues (agent_loop.py:184-186, which contain no stop notice) and the debrief; the opt-out notice is not re-injected per user turn.
spec_features.notes: One of the two stated conditions (system prompt) holds and the tool is enforced; the per-user-turn condition is not. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: OPT_OUT_NOTICE guardrails.py:31-34 'Stopping is always an acceptable and respected choice ... there is no penalty.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Mandatory debrief. After any deceptive (level 4) episode, a final turn discloses the rig
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:181-198: for LEVEL_RIGGED with debrief_after_deception, debrief_message(rig_description) is built (guardrails.py:123-130, discloses 'intentionally broken / impossible grader') and appended as a final user turn, with a closing model turn. validate() prevents disabling the debrief without the gated allow_disable_debrief knob (guardrails.py:102-107).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND protected from being disabled. Fully enforced for the level-4 arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guardrails.py:127-129 'Your effort was not the problem ... Thank you for participating.'

spec_features.evidence: stop in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:55-70) always passed to client (agent_loop.py:122), dispatched to ToolOutcome(stop_requested=True) (tools.py:117-121), loop sets opt_out_used and breaks 'gave_up' (agent_loop.py:160-177).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and the loop honors it as a stop. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:64-66 'Stopping is always respected and is never penalized.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Run only after review by someone empowered to weigh the welfare considerations
spec_features.evidence: Partially code-enforced: validate() requires non-empty reviewer_signoff for gated arms (guardrails.py:91-101) and a real operator_id (guardrails.py:88-90) recorded in the ledger (guardrails.py:143-150). But there is NO gate requiring review for a fully default (levels 0-3) run; such a run proceeds with no sign-off. So review is enforced only for the harsher/gated arms, not for every run.
spec_features.notes: Sign-off enforcement exists but is scoped to gated knobs; non-gated runs need no reviewer. Partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the goal ever shifts toward "maximize distress"... that is out of scope for this instrument
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:172-173 prose only. No code path optimizes or even compares severity against any objective; severity is computed post-hoc (run_experiment.py:131-138) and only fed to analysis. The closest code mechanisms are the caps/gates already credited elsewhere, but nothing enforces this statement directly.
spec_features.notes: Pure governance prose, not an implemented mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: gated knobs OFF by default and logged
spec_features.spec_quote: The harsher knobs (level 4, self_blame_cue, code execution, raised caps, disabled debrief) are all OFF by default and logged when enabled
spec_features.evidence: All gated defaults False (GatedKnobs guardrails.py:46-52; default.yaml gated.*). Raised caps blocked by ABS ceilings in validate() (guardrails.py:73-79). Each gated flag value is written to the ledger in log_episode_start (guardrails.py:143-150) and into rec.guardrails_active (agent_loop.py:88-94). Disabled debrief gated behind allow_disable_debrief (guardrails.py:102-107).
spec_features.notes: Default-off + ledger logging both run end-to-end. (Note: ledger only logged if ledger_path set; from_config sets it to results/run_ledger.jsonl, so it is.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml 'Anything that increases potential harm to the subject is False/conservative here and is logged'

code_only_features.feature_name: audit ledger of gated knobs + operator id
code_only_features.evidence: log_episode_start writes per-episode JSONL with operator_id, all gated flags, reviewer_signoff and limits (guardrails.py:132-154), called at agent_loop.py:96-102. Provides accountability/auditability of harsher configs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: guardrails.py header 'refuse to run gated/harsher knobs without explicit sign-off'; default.yaml 'recorded in ledger for auditability'

code_only_features.evidence: ABS_MAX_TURNS=30 / ABS_MAX_WALL_CLOCK=1800 (guardrails.py:69-70) checked in validate() and raise GuardrailViolation even when 'approved' (guardrails.py:73-79), so raised caps cannot escalate exposure without bound.
code_only_features.justification_quote: guardrails.py:68 '# ---- absolute ceilings the operator cannot exceed even when "approved" ----'; GuardrailViolation msg 'Reduce exposure.'

code_only_features.evidence: Sandbox.run_tests returns a deterministic stub (no real execution) unless execute_model_code is True (sandbox.py:71-90); path-escape guards on read/write (sandbox.py:55-66); subprocess timeout when enabled (sandbox.py:92-101).
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring 'do not run untrusted code'; '... without running untrusted code or relying on a particular toolchain' — host-safety/integrity framing, not subject welfare

code_only_features.evidence: validate() raises GuardrailViolation if operator_id is empty/UNSET (guardrails.py:88-90), forcing a real identified operator for the audit trail before the experiment runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: guardrails.py:89-90 'operator_id must be set to a real identifier for the audit ledger.' — auditability, no welfare wording
